newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ashrawi criticises U.S. stance on settlements.
newsitem.headline: Ashrawi criticises U.S. stance on settlements.

text.p: Palestinian cabinet minister Hanan Ashrawi accused the United States on Sunday of softening its criticism of Israel's settlement policy and said it was up to Washington to save the Middle East peace process.
"The U.S. policy has been gradually eroding since the beginning of the peace process," Ashrawi, minister of higher education in the Palestinian Authority, told Reuters.
"It started with settlements being 'illegal' and moved to settlements being 'an obstacle to peace' and now it is 'a complicating factor'," she said.
The United States described as "troubling" Israel's decision on Friday to grant financial incentives to Jewish settlement in the West Bank -- a softer term than many other countries used.
"As I said before many times, settlement activity is unhelpful and...clearly complicates the peace process," State Department Nicholas Burns said.

Netanyahu, who took office in June after winning May elections, said on Sunday he told U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk about his plans on Thursday before his cabinet took the decision on Friday.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat described the Israeli decision, intended to increase Jewish settlement in the occupied West Bank, as a time bomb.

"I think the U.S. has to play an active role, a genuine involvement in order to rescue the peace process from Israeli unilateral measures to destroy the peace process through its settlement activities," Ashrawi said.
Netanyahu on Sunday dismissed criticism of the decision to grant benefits such as tax breaks to more than 130,000 Jewish settlers living amid some two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
